claims.text: FDA boxed warning for a possible link with malignancy, though there is no firm evidence of one
claims.quote: Topical calcineurin inhibitors include an FDA boxed warning because of the possible association between the medications and malignancies, despite no firm evidence that there is a link.

claims.text: Steroid-sparing T-cell inhibitors for age two and older;
claims.quote: Topical calcineurin inhibitors are steroid-sparing immunomodulators used to treat atopic dermatitis in patients two years and older.

claims.text: may be used first-line with topical steroids, especially with steroid phobia or facial or flexural lesions; for short- or long-term use and maintenance
claims.quote: Although traditionally used as second-line treatment for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, they may be used as a first-line therapy in conjunction with topical steroids, especially in patients with steroid phobia (corticophobia), or facial or flexural lesions.30,34 Topical calcineurin inhibitors are recommended for short- or long-term use and for maintenance therapy.

claims.text: Pimecrolimus for mild to moderate disease, tacrolimus for moderate to severe (more effective);
claims.quote: Pimecrolimus is recommended for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, whereas tacrolimus is indicated for moderate to severe disease. Overall, tacrolimus is more effective than pimecrolimus, but both reduce inflammation and pruritus.
Tacrolimus ointment or pimecrolimus cream is applied 2 times a day.

claims.text: Proactive tacrolimus twice weekly on flare-prone areas reduces flares
claims.quote: A proactive maintenance approach of using tacrolimus twice weekly on areas prone to flare-ups reduces the rate of flare-ups and percentage of treatment days, and increases the time between flare-ups.

claims.text: No skin atrophy, so safe on face, eyelids, neck and groin.
claims.quote: Unlike topical steroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors do not cause skin atrophy and can be safely applied to areas with thinner skin, such as the face (including eyelids), neck, and groin.
Burning or stinging after application is usually transient and abates after a few days.

claims.text: is the most common adverse effect
claims.quote: Localized reactions, including burning, stinging, and pruritus, are the most common adverse effects.
